claim: Eukaryotic genomes are packaged into chromatin, a structure defined by repeating units of ~147 bp of DNA wrapped around a protein complex known as the nucleosome.
source: Eukaryotic genomes are packaged into chromatin, a structure defined by repeating units of ~147 bp of DNA wrapped around a protein complex known as the nucleosome (Luger et al., 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Luger et al., 1997, which is a foundational reference in the field.

claim: Nucleosomes contain two copies of each of the core histones H2A, H2B, H3, and H4.
source: Nucleosomes contain two copies of each of the core histones H2A, H2B, H3, and H4.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about nucleosome composition.

claim: Dozens of histone variants in the H2A, H2B, and H3 families have been identified in eukaryotes.
source: Histone variants have arisen through the divergence of their intrinsically disordered loop and tail regions and dozens of histone variants in the H2A, H2B, and H3 families have been identified in eukaryotes (Loppin and Berger, 2020; Talbert and Henikoff, 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Loppin and Berger, 2020 and Talbert and Henikoff, 2021.

claim: Histone variants regulate the properties of nucleosomes.
source: These variants regulate the properties of nucleosomes (Chakravarthy et al., 2004; Horikoshi et al., 2013; Koyama and Kurumizaka, 2018; Tachiwana et al., 2012)
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to studies demonstrating the regulatory effects of histone variants.

claim: Histone variants affect transcription.
source: These variants regulate the properties of nucleosomes (Chakravarthy et al., 2004; Horikoshi et al., 2013; Koyama and Kurumizaka, 2018; Tachiwana et al., 2012) and affect transcription (Rudnizky et al., 2016; Subramanian et al., 2015; Weber and Henikoff, 2014; Wollmann et al., 2012; Wollmann et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to studies showing effects on transcription.

claim: Animals and plants have evolved unique H2A variants associated with transcriptional repression.
source: Animals and plants have evolved unique H2A variants associated with transcriptional repression (Loppin and Berger, 2020; Talbert and Henikoff, 2021) and with gametes (Osakabe and Molaro, 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Loppin and Berger, 2020 and Talbert and Henikoff, 2021.

claim: In vascular plants, the H2A.W variants are distinguished by a C-terminal KSPK motif.
source: In vascular plants, the H2A.W variants are distinguished by a C-terminal KSPK motif (Lei et al., 2021; Bourguet et al., 2021; Yelagandula et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Lei et al., 2021, Bourguet et al., 2021, and Yelagandula et al., 2014.

claim: In synergy with H3K9 methylation, H2A.W favors heterochromatic silencing by directly altering the interaction between H2A.W and DNA.
source: In synergy with H3K9 methylation, H2A.W favors heterochromatic silencing by directly altering the interaction between H2A.W and DNA (Bourguet et al., 2021; Osakabe et al., 2021; Bourguet et al., 2021; Yelagandula et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple studies on H2A.W function.

claim: The roles of the recently recognized H2B variants in transcription remains unknown.
source: The roles of the recently recognized H2B variants (Jiang et al., 2020; Raman et al., 2022) in transcription remains unknown.
evidence: This claim acknowledges a gap in knowledge while citing recent work identifying H2B variants.

claim: H2B variants might differ in their capacity to be ubiquitinated, an important modification for RNA polymerase II elongation.
source: However, H2B variants might differ in their capacity to be ubiquitinated, an important modification for RNA polymerase II elongation (Feng and Shen, 2014; Kim et al., 2009; Minsky et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a speculative claim ('might differ') supported by citations about the importance of H2B ubiquitination.

claim: Applying a Hidden Markov Model (ChromHMM) to genomic profiles of histone modifications revealed chromatin states in mammals, Drosophila, Arabidopsis, and rice.
source: Applying a Hidden Markov Model (ChromHMM) (Ernst and Kellis, 2012; Ernst and Kellis, 2017) to genomic profiles of histone modifications revealed chromatin states that reflect the combination of post-transcriptional histone modifications present in mammals, Drosophila, Arabidopsis, and rice (Ernst and Kellis, 2012; Ernst and Kellis, 2017; Kharchenko et al., 2011; Liu et al., 2018; Roudier et al., 2011; Sequeira-Mendes et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to studies using ChromHMM in various organisms.

claim: Chromatin states distinguish the major domains of chromatin within the genome, comprising euchromatin (with active genes), facultative heterochromatin (with repressed genes), and constitutive heterochromatin (with transposons and repeats) in animals and plants.
source: Chromatin states distinguish the major domains of chromatin within the genome, comprising euchromatin (with active genes), facultative heterochromatin (with repressed genes), and constitutive heterochromatin (with transposons and repeats) in animals and plants.
evidence: This is established knowledge about chromatin organization based on the ChromHMM studies cited in the previous sentence.

claim: In Arabidopsis, there is a clear correlation between transcript levels and enrichment of the variant H3.3 on gene bodies marked by H3K36me2.
source: In Arabidopsis, there is a clear correlation between transcript levels and enrichment of the variant H3.3 (Stroud et al., 2012; Wollmann et al., 2012; Wollmann et al., 2017) and H2A and H2A.X (Yelagandula et al., 2014) on gene bodies marked by H3K36me2 (Leng et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple studies showing correlations between H3.3 and transcription.

claim: H2A.Z is enriched on repressed genes marked by H3K27me3.
source: In contrast, H2A.Z is enriched on repressed genes marked by H3K27me3 (Carter et al., 2018)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Carter et al., 2018.

claim: The histone variant H2A.W is present on transposons and repeats marked by H3K9me2.
source: and the histone variant H2A.W is present on transposons and repeats marked by H3K9me2 (Osakabe et al., 2021; Yelagandula et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Osakabe et al., 2021 and Yelagandula et al., 2014.

claim: In Arabidopsis, homotypic nucleosomes containing a single type of H2A variant are prevalent.
source: In Arabidopsis, homotypic nucleosomes containing a single type of H2A variant are prevalent (Osakabe et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Osakabe et al., 2018.

claim: ~60% of H3.1 nucleosomes contained both H3.1 and H3.3 variants.
source: Spectral counts of peptides covering regions around lysine 27 (K27), where H3.1 and H3.3 can be distinguished by MS analysis, revealed that ~60% of H3.1 and ~42% of H3.3 nucleosomes contained both H3 variants, (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data presented in Figure 1A.

claim: ~42% of H3.3 nucleosomes contained both H3.1 and H3.3 variants.
source: Spectral counts of peptides covering regions around lysine 27 (K27), where H3.1 and H3.3 can be distinguished by MS analysis, revealed that ~60% of H3.1 and ~42% of H3.3 nucleosomes contained both H3 variants, (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data presented in Figure 1A.

claim: Neither H3.1 nor H3.3 was preferentially associated with a specific H2A variant.
source: We analyzed H3.1 and H3.3 nucleosomes for the presence of H2A variants by western blotting and found that neither H3.1 nor H3.3 was preferentially associated with a specific H2A variant (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blotting data presented in Figure 1B.

claim: H3 variants do not necessarily form homotypic nucleosomes, despite the presence of H3 variant-specific deposition mechanisms.
source: Thus, by contrast with H2A variants, H3 variants do not necessarily form homotypic nucleosomes, despite the presence of H3 variant-specific deposition mechanisms (Loppin and Berger, 2020; Nie et al., 2014; Probst, 2022), and they do not associate with a specific H2A variant.
evidence: This claim is supported by the data presented in the manuscript and citations to studies on H3 deposition mechanisms.

claim: H3 variants do not associate with a specific H2A variant.
source: Thus, by contrast with H2A variants, H3 variants do not necessarily form homotypic nucleosomes, despite the presence of H3 variant-specific deposition mechanisms (Loppin and Berger, 2020; Nie et al., 2014; Probst, 2022), and they do not associate with a specific H2A variant.
evidence: This claim is supported by the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: All the methylation and acetylation marks surveyed were present on transgenic and endogenous H3 in both H3.1 and H3.3 immunoprecipitations.
source: We found that all the methylation and acetylation marks surveyed were present on transgenic (T) and endogenous (E) H3 in both H3.1 and H3.3 immunoprecipitations (Figure 1C)
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data presented in Figure 1C.

claim: There was some degree of preferential association of H3K4me, H3K36me, and H3 acetylation with H3.3.
source: although there was some degree of preferential association of H3K4me, H3K36me, and H3 acetylation with H3.3 and of H3K27me1 with H3.1 (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data presented in Figure 1C.

claim: There was some degree of preferential association of H3K27me1 with H3.1.
source: although there was some degree of preferential association of H3K4me, H3K36me, and H3 acetylation with H3.3 and of H3K27me1 with H3.1 (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data presented in Figure 1C.

claim: Similar levels of H3K27me2 and H3K27me3 marks were identified on both H3.1 and H3.3.
source: In contrast to previous reports (Johnson et al., 2004; Zhang et al., 2007) we identified similar levels of H3K27me2 and H3K27me3 marks on both H3.1 and H3.3 whereas the constitutive heterochromatin mark H3K27me1 was higher on H3.1 (Figure 1D and E; Figure 1—figure supplement 1E-G).
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data presented in Figure 1D, E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1E-G, and contrasts with previous reports.

claim: The constitutive heterochromatin mark H3K27me1 was higher on H3.1.
source: In contrast to previous reports (Johnson et al., 2004; Zhang et al., 2007) we identified similar levels of H3K27me2 and H3K27me3 marks on both H3.1 and H3.3 whereas the constitutive heterochromatin mark H3K27me1 was higher on H3.1 (Figure 1D and E; Figure 1—figure supplement 1E-G).
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data presented in Figure 1D, E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1E-G.

claim: High levels of H3K27me1 on H3.3 are the likely product of the demethylation of H3K27me3 by the JUMONJI H3K27 demethylases or intermediates of methylation by the Polycomb Repressive Complex 2.
source: High levels of H3K27me1 on H3.3 were unexpected considering the specificity of H3K27 methyltransferases ATXR5/6 for H3.1 (Jacob et al., 2014) and are the likely product of the demethylation of H3K27me3 by the JUMONJI H3K27 demethylases (Gan et al., 2015; Liu et al., 2010) or intermediates of methylation by the Polycomb Repressive Complex 2.
evidence: This is a speculative claim ('likely product') supported by citations to studies on H3K27 methylation and demethylation.

claim: Acetylation and all three methylation states at H3K36 that are associated with active chromatin were found on both H3.1 and H3.3 but with higher enrichment on H3.3.
source: Acetylation and all three methylation states at H3K36 that are associated with active chromatin were likewise found on both H3.1 and H3.3 but with higher enrichment on H3.3 (Figure 1D and E; Figure 1—figure supplement 1E-G).
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data presented in Figure 1D, E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1E-G.

claim: The levels of H3K27 and H3K36 modifications on H3.1 and H3.3 displayed the same trends irrespective of whether they were precipitated with either H3.1 or H3.3 nucleosomes.
source: The levels of H3K27 and H3K36 modifications on H3.1 and H3.3 displayed the same trends irrespective of whether they were precipitated with either H3.1 or H3.3 nucleosomes, contrasting with the predominant enrichment of H3K37 modifications on H3.3 (Figure 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data presented in Figure 1E.

claim: H3K37 modifications are predominantly enriched on H3.3.
source: The levels of H3K27 and H3K36 modifications on H3.1 and H3.3 displayed the same trends irrespective of whether they were precipitated with either H3.1 or H3.3 nucleosomes, contrasting with the predominant enrichment of H3K37 modifications on H3.3 (Figure 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data presented in Figure 1E.

claim: H3K9me1 and H3K9me2 were similarly distributed among H3.1 and H3.3.
source: Therefore, we analyzed H3K9me1 and H3K9me2, which mark constitutive heterochromatin in plants, only on transgenic H3 and found that both marks were similarly distributed among H3.1 and H3.3 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1H) as reported previously (Johnson et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data presented in Figure 1—figure supplement 1H and a citation to Johnson et al., 2004.

claim: Acetylation of H3K9, H3K14, H3K18, H3K23 and combinations thereof were very similar in H3.1 and H3.3 immunoprecipitations.
source: Also, acetylation of H3K9, H3K14, H3K18, H3K23 and combinations thereof were very similar in H3.1 and H3.3 immunoprecipitations (Figure 1—figure supplement 1I-K).
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data presented in Figure 1—figure supplement 1I-K.

claim: The vast majority of H3 modifications are not H3 variant specific to the notable exception of H3K36 and H3K37 modifications that are associated preferentially but not uniquely with H3.3.
source: As the total numbers of measured spectra covering H3 modifications were nearly identical for H3.1 and H3.3 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F) our MS together with western blot data suggest that the vast majority of H3 modifications are not H3 variant specific to the notable exception of H3K36 and H3K37 modifications that are associated preferentially but not uniquely with H3.3.
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry and western blot data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The preference for H3K36 and H3K37 modifications on H3.3 might be related to the presence of substitutions at position 41 specific that distinguishes H3.1 from H3.3 in plants.
source: This preference for H3.3 might be related to the presence of substitutions at position 41 specific that distinguishes H3.1 from H3.3 in plants (Borg et al., 2021; Probst, 2022).
evidence: This is a speculative claim ('might be related') supported by citations to studies on H3 variants in plants.

claim: In the heterotypic nucleosomes the same modifications are found on either H3 variants present irrespective of their identity.
source: These findings suggested that in the heterotypic nucleosomes the same modifications are found on either H3 variants present irrespective of their identity.
evidence: This is an inference based on the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Homotypic nucleosomes containing either H2A.W, H2A.Z, H2A, or H2A.X showed marked enrichment of specific histone modifications.
source: Unlike H3 variants, homotypic nucleosomes containing either H2A.W, H2A.Z, H2A, or H2A.X showed marked enrichment of specific histone modifications (Figure 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data presented in Figure 1F.

claim: Histone modifications in constitutive heterochromatin (H3K9me1, H3K9me2, and H3K27me1) were primarily associated with H2A.W.
source: Histone modifications in constitutive heterochromatin (H3K9me1, H3K9me2, and H3K27me1) were primarily associated with H2A.W consistent with their synergistic impact on silencing transposons (Bourguet et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by data in the manuscript and a citation to Bourguet et al., 2021.

claim: The modification H3K27me3 (facultative heterochromatin) was detected only in H2A.Z nucleosomes.
source: The modification H3K27me3 (facultative heterochromatin) was detected only in H2A.Z nucleosomes
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in the manuscript.

claim: H3K36me3 (marking euchromatin) was primarily detected in H2A, H2A.X, and H2A.Z nucleosomes.
source: and H3K36me3 (marking euchromatin) was primarily detected in H2A, H2A.X, and H2A.Z nucleosomes.
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in the manuscript.

claim: H3K4me1 and H3K4me3 co-precipitated high levels of H3K27me1, H3K27me3, and H3K36me3 and low levels of H3K9me1 and H3K9me2.
source: Surprisingly, H3K4me1 and H3K4me3 co-precipitated high levels of H3K27me1, H3K27me3, and H3K36me3 and low levels of H3K9me1 and H3K9me2 (Figure 1F) showing that repressive and active H3 marks co-exist on the same nucleosomes or potentially on the same H3 tail.
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data presented in Figure 1F.

claim: Repressive and active H3 marks co-exist on the same nucleosomes or potentially on the same H3 tail.
source: Surprisingly, H3K4me1 and H3K4me3 co-precipitated high levels of H3K27me1, H3K27me3, and H3K36me3 and low levels of H3K9me1 and H3K9me2 (Figure 1F) showing that repressive and active H3 marks co-exist on the same nucleosomes or potentially on the same H3 tail.
evidence: This is an inference based on the co-precipitation data presented in Figure 1F.

claim: Similar complex interplay between H3 marks has also been observed in mouse ES cells.
source: Similar complex interplay between H3 marks has also been observed in mouse ES cells (Schwämmle et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Schwämmle et al., 2016.

claim: H2A but not H3 variants form homotypic nucleosomes that preferentially carry specific histone modifications associated with either the transcriptional status of protein-coding genes or transposons.
source: Therefore, H2A but not H3 variants form homotypic nucleosomes that preferentially carry specific histone modifications associated with either the transcriptional status of protein-coding genes or transposons.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The 26 chromatin states model proved to be most parsimonious.
source: We chose to analyze the 26 chromatin states model, which proved to be most parsimonious (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A; see Methods).
evidence: This claim is supported by the analysis presented in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A and the Methods section.

claim: Chromatin states H1–H6 showed low accessibility, the highest levels of DNA methylation, and primarily occupied transcriptionally inactive transposons and repeats, thus representing constitutive heterochromatin.
source: Chromatin states H1–H6 showed low accessibility, the highest levels of DNA methylation, and primarily occupied transcriptionally inactive transposons and repeats, thus representing constitutive heterochromatin.
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in the manuscript showing characteristics of these chromatin states.

claim: The states F1–F6 were associated with low transcriptional activity and were present over genes and pseudogenes, indicating that they represented facultative heterochromatin.
source: The states F1–F6 were associated with low transcriptional activity and were present over genes and pseudogenes, indicating that they represented facultative heterochromatin.
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in the manuscript showing characteristics of these chromatin states.

claim: Constitutive and facultative heterochromatin composed 17% and 20% of the genome, respectively.
source: As defined by state occupancy, constitutive and facultative heterochromatin composed 17% and 20% of the genome, respectively (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B), corresponding to previous estimates (Roudier et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B and a citation to Roudier et al., 2011.

claim: The states E1–E11 occupied expressed genes and thus comprised euchromatin.
source: The states E1–E11 occupied expressed genes and thus comprised euchromatin.
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in the manuscript showing characteristics of these chromatin states.

claim: Three states (I1–I3) showed the lowest nucleosome density and highest accessibility and occupied a large fraction of non-coding RNAs and a quarter of untranslated regions of genes (3′UTR and 5′UTR).
source: Three states (I1–I3) showed the lowest nucleosome density and highest accessibility and occupied a large fraction of non-coding RNAs (Figure 2—figure supplement 2G) and a quarter of untranslated regions of genes (3′UTR and 5′UTR) (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 2G.

claim: The states I1–I3 were classified as intergenic.
source: Hence, the states I1–I3 were classified as intergenic.
evidence: This is a classification based on the characteristics of these states presented in the manuscript.

claim: Specific groups of chromatin states define constitutive heterochromatin (H1-6), facultative heterochromatin (F1-6), euchromatin (E1-11), and intergenic regions (I1-3).
source: We conclude that specific groups of chromatin states define constitutive heterochromatin (H1-6), facultative heterochromatin (F1-6), euchromatin (E1-11), and intergenic regions (I1-3).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The chromatin states recapitulate the preferential associations between H2A variants and histone modifications observed in mononucleosomes.
source: Overall, the chromatin states recapitulate the preferential associations between H2A variants and histone modifications observed in mononucleosomes (Figure 1; Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by comparing the chromatin states with the mononucleosome data presented in Figure 1.

claim: H2A.W and H3K9me1 are the determining marks of all six heterochromatic states.
source: H2A.W and H3K9me1 are the determining marks of all six heterochromatic states.
evidence: This claim is supported by the chromatin state analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: H2A.Z, with the polycomb histone modifications H2AK121ub and H3K27me3, are the hallmark of facultative heterochromatin states.
source: H2A.Z, with the polycomb histone modifications H2AK121ub and H3K27me3, are the hallmark of facultative heterochromatin states.
evidence: This claim is supported by the chromatin state analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: H2A and H2A.X associated with H2Bub and H3K36me3 mark euchromatic states.
source: H2A and H2A.X associated with H2Bub and H3K36me3 mark euchromatic states.
evidence: This claim is supported by the chromatin state analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: Much less prominent associations are observed between histone modifications and either H3 or H2B variants compared to H2A variants.
source: Contrasting with the strong association between H2A variants and the three major domains of chromatin, much less prominent associations are observed between histone modifications and either H3 or H2B variants.
evidence: This claim is supported by the chromatin state analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: The blocks of heterochromatic states H1–H6 corresponded to the previously identified states 8 and 9, which were also defined as heterochromatin in a previous study.
source: The blocks of heterochromatic states H1–H6 corresponded to the previously identified states 8 and 9, which were also defined as heterochromatin in a previous study (Sequeira-Mendes et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison with a previous study cited.

claim: The addition of the comprehensive set of histone variants in the 26-state model provides a more refined and coherent classification of elements of chromatin than the 9-state model defined primarily based on chromatin modifications and the variants H3.1 and H3.3.
source: Altogether, the addition of the comprehensive set of histone variants in the 26-state model provides a more refined and coherent classification of elements of chromatin than the 9-state model defined primarily based on chromatin modifications and the variants H3.1 and H3.3, suggesting the importance of histone variants in the definition of chromatin states.
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison of the two models presented in the manuscript.

claim: Removing H2B variants did not affect most chromatin states, except for H1 and I2.
source: Removing H2B variants did not affect most chromatin states, except for H1 and I2, which showed high emissions probabilities for H2B variants (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by the sub-epigenome model analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: H3 variants showed larger contributions in defining specific states compared to H2B variants.
source: In contrast, H3 variants showed larger contributions in defining specific states
evidence: This claim is supported by the sub-epigenome model analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: Removing all H2A variants caused the loss of several states marked by a Jaccard index <0.7.
source: and removing all H2A variants caused the loss of several states marked by a Jaccard index <0.7 (Figure 2F).
evidence: This claim is supported by the sub-epigenome model analysis presented in Figure 2F.

claim: Removing all histone variants had a stronger impact than removing all H3 modifications from the model.
source: Eventually, removing all histone variants had a stronger impact than removing all H3 modifications from the model.
evidence: This claim is supported by the sub-epigenome model analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: Among histone variants, H2A variants have the strongest effect on defining the chromatin states by their association with histone modifications.
source: In summary, our computational and biochemical analyses led to conclude that, among histone variants, H2A variants have the strongest effect on defining the chromatin states by their association with histone modifications.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the computational and biochemical analyses presented in the manuscript.

claim: In the ddm1 mutant, TEs show a loss of DNA methylation, H3K9 methylation, and linker histone H1 as well as an increase in H3K27me3.
source: In the ddm1 mutant, TEs show a loss of DNA methylation, H3K9 methylation, and linker histone H1 as well as an increase in H3K27me3 (Jeddeloh et al., 1998; Kakutani et al., 1999; Osakabe et al., 2021; Rougée et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple studies on the ddm1 mutant.

claim: DDM1 causes the deposition of H2A.W.6 to heterochromatin.
source: This study showed that DDM1 causes the deposition of H2A.W.6 to heterochromatin
evidence: This claim is supported by a previous study by the authors.

claim: Neither tissue type nor developmental stage has a dramatic effect on the definition of chromatin states in the wild-type.
source: This indicated that neither tissue type nor developmental stage has a dramatic effect on the definition of chromatin states in the wild-type.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the concatenated model analysis comparing seedlings and leaves.

claim: The loss of DDM1 causes a profound perturbation of the chromatin states associated with constitutive heterochromatin.
source: Hence, the loss of DDM1 broadly affected the association of chromatin states with regions covered with constitutive heterochromatin in the wild-type.
evidence: This claim is supported by the chromatin state analysis of ddm1 presented in the manuscript.

claim: ddm1 did not significantly affect the group similarity for facultative heterochromatin and euchromatin states.
source: Overall, ddm1 caused a perturbation of the chromatin states associated with constitutive heterochromatin and did not significantly affect the group similarity for facultative heterochromatin and euchromatin states between the 16- and 26- state models, with genomic overlaps between 68 and 100% for the non-mixed states (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by the chromatin state analysis of ddm1 presented in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The constitutive heterochromatin present over TEs in wild-type was replaced in ddm1 by chromatin states found in intergenic, facultative heterochromatin, and euchromatin in wild-type.
source: Overall, the constitutive heterochromatin present over TEs in wild-type was replaced in ddm1 by chromatin states found in intergenic, facultative heterochromatin, and euchromatin in wild-type (Figure 3E and F; Figure 3—figure supplement 1E, F).
evidence: This claim is supported by the chromatin state analysis of ddm1 presented in Figure 3E, F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1E, F.

claim: ddm1 affected not only constitutive heterochromatin but also regions of euchromatin and facultative heterochromatin that adopted chromatin states distinct from these found in the wild-type.
source: In addition, we observed that ddm1 affected not only constitutive heterochromatin but also regions of euchromatin and facultative heterochromatin that adopted chromatin states distinct from these found in the wild-type. suggesting indirect effects of the disruption of constitutive heterochromatin caused directly by the loss of DDM1 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by the chromatin state analysis of ddm1 presented in Figure 3—figure supplement 1F.

claim: The loss of DDM1 causes a profound perturbation of both the definition of chromatin states and their distribution.
source: We thus concluded that the loss of DDM1 causes a profound perturbation of both the definition of chromatin states and their distribution.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the chromatin state analysis of ddm1 presented in the manuscript.

claim: DDM1 specifically binds H2A.W but neither H2A.X nor H1 linker histones.
source: We have previously shown that DDM1 specifically binds H2A.W but neither H2A.X nor H1 linker histones (Osakabe et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study by the authors.

claim: His6-tagged DDM1 co-precipitated heterodimers containing H2A.W and H2A.Z but not H2A or H2A.X.
source: We found that His6-tagged DDM1 co-precipitated heterodimers containing H2A.W and H2A.Z but not H2A or H2A.X (Figure 3G).
evidence: This claim is supported by pull-down assay data presented in Figure 3G.

claim: DDM1 bound H2A.W and H2A.Z but not H2A and H2A.X.
source: This demonstrated that DDM1 bound H2A.W and H2A.Z but not H2A and H2A.X.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the pull-down assay data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The C-terminal tail of H2A.W was dispensable for DDM1 binding.
source: Notably, the C-terminal tail of H2A.W was dispensable for DDM1 binding (Figure 3G).
evidence: This claim is supported by pull-down assay data presented in Figure 3G.

claim: Fragments containing residues 100–123 or 639–673 were able to bind H2A.W and H2A.Z.
source: Our pulldown assays showed that fragments containing residues 100–123 or 639–673 were able to bind H2A.W and H2A.Z, whereas some additional regions of DDM1 showed weak binding only to H2A.Z (Figure 3H; Figure 3—figure supplement 2A-C).
evidence: This claim is supported by pull-down assay data presented in Figure 3H and Figure 3—figure supplement 2A-C.

claim: DDM1 uses the same conserved sites to bind H2A.Z and H2A.W.
source: Thus, DDM1 uses the same conserved sites to bind H2A.Z and H2A.W.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the pull-down assay data presented in the manuscript.

claim: H2A.W evolved in land plants independently from macroH2A in animals.
source: H2A.W evolved in land plants independently from macroH2A in animals (Osakabe and Molaro, 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Osakabe and Molaro, 2023.

claim: macroH2A is also associated with heterochromatin although not as strictly as H2A.W.
source: macroH2A is also associated with heterochromatin although not as strictly as H2A.W (Sun and Bernstein, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Sun and Bernstein, 2019.

claim: The deposition of macroH2A depends at least in part on the DDM1 murine ortholog LSH.
source: The deposition of macroH2A depends at least in part on the DDM1 murine ortholog LSH (Ni et al., 2020)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Ni et al., 2020.

claim: It was proposed that LSH binds and exchanges H2A to macroH2A.
source: and it was proposed that LSH binds and exchanges H2A to macroH2A (Ni and Muegge, 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Ni and Muegge, 2021.

claim: An overall enrichment of H2A.Z over TE genes in ddm1 was observed.
source: We observed an overall enrichment of H2A.Z over TE genes in ddm1, supporting the idea that DDM1 promotes the removal of H2A.Z at TE genes where DDM1 deposits H2A.W in the wild-type (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data presented in Figure 4A.

claim: DDM1 promotes the removal of H2A.Z at TE genes where DDM1 deposits H2A.W in the wild-type.
source: We observed an overall enrichment of H2A.Z over TE genes in ddm1, supporting the idea that DDM1 promotes the removal of H2A.Z at TE genes where DDM1 deposits H2A.W in the wild-type (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is an inference based on the ChIP-seq data presented in Figure 4A.

claim: Non-transcribed TE genes also accumulated H2A.Z in ddm1.
source: Remarkably, non-transcribed TE genes also accumulated H2A.Z (Figure 4A) supporting the conclusion that the replacement of H2A.W by H2A.Z observed in ddm1 mutants is not governed by transcription.
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data presented in Figure 4A.

claim: The replacement of H2A.W by H2A.Z observed in ddm1 mutants is not governed by transcription.
source: Remarkably, non-transcribed TE genes also accumulated H2A.Z (Figure 4A) supporting the conclusion that the replacement of H2A.W by H2A.Z observed in ddm1 mutants is not governed by transcription.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the ChIP-seq data showing H2A.Z accumulation on non-transcribed TEs.

claim: Transcribed TE genes showed enrichment in H2A.Z at their TSS.
source: Transcribed TE genes showed enrichment in H2A.Z at their TSS (Figure 4A) but also H2A.X on the gene body (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data presented in Figure 4A.

claim: Transcribed TE genes showed enrichment in H2A.X on the gene body.
source: Transcribed TE genes showed enrichment in H2A.Z at their TSS (Figure 4A) but also H2A.X on the gene body (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data presented in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Transcription of TEs in ddm1 did not affect the degree of enrichment for H3K27me3 of facultative heterochromatin.
source: Transcription of TEs in ddm1 did not affect the degree of enrichment for H3K27me3 of facultative heterochromatin but with increasing levels of transcription, there was increased enrichment of H3K36me3, resulting in a chromatin profile typical of expressed protein-coding genes (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data presented in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: With increasing levels of transcription of TEs in ddm1, there was increased enrichment of H3K36me3, resulting in a chromatin profile typical of expressed protein-coding genes.
source: Transcription of TEs in ddm1 did not affect the degree of enrichment for H3K27me3 of facultative heterochromatin but with increasing levels of transcription, there was increased enrichment of H3K36me3, resulting in a chromatin profile typical of expressed protein-coding genes (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data presented in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Strongly expressed TE genes showed an accumulation of euchromatic states in ddm1.
source: Accordingly, strongly expressed TE genes showed an accumulation of euchromatic states, in contrast with non-expressed TE genes that became covered with states typical of facultative heterochromatin, irrespective of the type of constitutive heterochromatin observed on these TE genes in wild-type (Figure 4B and C; Figure 4—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by chromatin state analysis data presented in Figure 4B, C and Figure 4—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Non-expressed TE genes became covered with states typical of facultative heterochromatin in ddm1, irrespective of the type of constitutive heterochromatin observed on these TE genes in wild-type.
source: Accordingly, strongly expressed TE genes showed an accumulation of euchromatic states, in contrast with non-expressed TE genes that became covered with states typical of facultative heterochromatin, irrespective of the type of constitutive heterochromatin observed on these TE genes in wild-type (Figure 4B and C; Figure 4—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by chromatin state analysis data presented in Figure 4B, C and Figure 4—figure supplement 2A.

claim: At TE genes, DDM1 prevents the replacement of H2A.W by H2A.Z in a transcription-independent manner.
source: We conclude that at TE genes, DDM1 prevents the replacement of H2A.W by H2A.Z in a transcription-independent manner.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the data presented in the manuscript showing H2A.Z accumulation on non-transcribed TEs in ddm1.

claim: The alteration in the dynamics of H2A.W and H2A.Z in ddm1 perturbs the allocation of chromatin states at constitutive heterochromatin and in other regions of chromatin.
source: Yet, the alteration in the dynamics of H2A.W and H2A.Z in ddm1 perturbs the allocation of chromatin states at constitutive heterochromatin and in other regions of chromatin.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the chromatin state analysis of ddm1 presented in the manuscript.

claim: When TEs are strongly expressed in ddm1, they acquire euchromatin states marked by H2A and H2A.X over their gene body, while H2A.Z remains confined to the transcription start site.
source: In some TEs, the new chromatin state acquired in ddm1 permits transcription, which is then accompanied by a further exchange of H2A.Z to H2A and H2A.X and further loss of marks of constitutive heterochromatin and H1 and gain of marks of euchromatin (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data presented in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Histone modifications and histone variants combine into chromatin states that subdivide the intergenic space, the non-protein-coding space, and the protein-coding genic space of the genome into biologically significant subunits.
source: We report that histone modifications and histone variants combine into chromatin states that subdivide the intergenic space, the non-protein-coding space, and the protein-coding genic space of the genome into biologically significant subunits.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the chromatin state analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: These chromatin states summarize the prevalent organization of chromatin across cell types and stages of vegetative development from seedlings to mature leaves.
source: These chromatin states summarize the prevalent organization of chromatin across cell types and stages of vegetative development from seedlings to mature leaves.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the concatenated model analysis comparing seedlings and leaves.

claim: Minor variations in chromatin states occur between vegetative cell types.
source: Our data suggest that minor variations in chromatin states occur between vegetative cell types.
evidence: This is an inference based on the concatenated model analysis comparing seedlings and leaves.

claim: Highly specialized cell types such as gametes with specific histone variants and unusually high or low levels of chromatin regulators harbor specific chromatin states that are not reflected in our study.
source: We predict that highly specialized cell types such as gametes (Borg et al., 2020; Borg et al., 2021) with specific histone variants and unusually high or low levels of chromatin regulators harbor specific chromatin states that are not reflected in our study.
evidence: This is a speculative prediction based on knowledge of specialized cell types.

claim: Calculation of chromatin states and biochemical analyses demonstrate the strongest associations between nucleosomes homotypic for H2A variants and histone modifications.
source: Calculation of chromatin states and biochemical analyses demonstrate the strongest associations between nucleosomes homotypic for H2A variants and histone modifications while nucleosomes are primarily heterotypic for H3 variants with a weaker association with histone modifications.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the chromatin state and biochemical analyses presented in the manuscript.

claim: Nucleosomes are primarily heterotypic for H3 variants with a weaker association with histone modifications.
source: Calculation of chromatin states and biochemical analyses demonstrate the strongest associations between nucleosomes homotypic for H2A variants and histone modifications while nucleosomes are primarily heterotypic for H3 variants with a weaker association with histone modifications.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the chromatin state and biochemical analyses presented in the manuscript.

claim: The prominent role of H2A variants in the organization of chromatin states is supported by systematic evaluation of the individual contribution of histone variants, H3 marks, and a combination thereof.
source: The prominent role of H2A variants in the organization of chromatin states is supported by systematic evaluation of the individual contribution of histone variants, H3 marks, and a combination thereof (Figure 2F) and the impact of the loss of the remodeler DDM1, which deposits H2A.W to maintain TE silencing (Osakabe et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by the sub-epigenome model analysis presented in Figure 2F and the ddm1 analysis.

claim: The DDM1 binding sites for H2A.W also bind H2A.Z, but not H2A or H2A.X.
source: We further show that the DDM1 binding sites for H2A.W also bind H2A.Z, but not H2A or H2A.X.
evidence: This claim is supported by the pull-down assay data presented in the manuscript.

claim: In ddm1, we observe a net replacement of H2A.W by H2A.Z.
source: In ddm1, we observe a net replacement of H2A.W by H2A.Z.
evidence: This claim is supported by the ChIP-seq data presented in the manuscript.

claim: DDM1 could exchange directly H2A.Z to H2A.W.
source: DDM1 could exchange directly H2A.Z to H2A.W.
evidence: This is a speculative model proposed by the authors.

claim: The convergent evolution of DDM1 and its orthologs LSH and HELLS in mammals with LSH catalyzing the exchange between replication dependent H2A and macroH2A supports the idea that DDM1 exchanges H2A.Z to H2A.W.
source: This model would support the idea of the convergent evolution of DDM1 and its orthologs LSH and HELLS in mammals with LSH catalyzing the exchange between replication dependent H2A and macroH2A (Berger et al., 2023; Ni and Muegge, 2021).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation supported by citations to studies on LSH.

claim: The replacement of H2A.W by H2A.Z might be indirect in ddm1.
source: An alternative model is that the replacement of H2A.W by H2A.Z is indirect in ddm1.
evidence: This is an alternative speculative model proposed by the authors.

claim: H2A.Z might be deposited because of the loss of DNA methylation in ddm1, which is consistent with the well-established mutually exclusive patterns of H2A.Z and DNA methylation.
source: For example, H2A.Z might be deposited because of the loss of DNA methylation in ddm1, which is consistent with the well-established mutually exclusive patterns of H2A.Z and DNA methylation (Zilberman et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a speculative explanation supported by a citation to Zilberman et al., 2008.

claim: It is unlikely that on its own, the loss of H2A.W in ddm1 causes the deposition of H2A.Z on constitutive heterochromatin because this is not observed in mutants lacking H2A.W.
source: Whichever mechanism is involved it is unlikely that on its own, the loss of H2A.W in ddm1 causes the deposition of H2A.Z on constitutive heterochromatin because this is not observed in mutants lacking H2A.W (Bourguet et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Bourguet et al., 2021.

claim: The resulting enrichment of H2A.Z in ddm1 is accompanied by a corresponding exchange of constitutive to facultative chromatin states over TEs.
source: The resulting enrichment of H2A.Z in ddm1 is accompanied by a corresponding exchange of constitutive to facultative chromatin states over TEs.
evidence: This claim is supported by the chromatin state analysis of ddm1 presented in the manuscript.

claim: TEs that remain silent in ddm1 are occupied by a facultative heterochromatin marked by H2A.Z and H3K27me3.
source: Notably, this does not require transcription, as TEs that remain silent in ddm1 are likewise occupied by a facultative heterochromatin marked by H2A.Z and H3K27me3.
evidence: This claim is supported by the chromatin state and ChIP-seq analysis of ddm1 presented in the manuscript.

claim: H2A variants appear to be important in shaping the deposition of histone modifications and defining chromatin states.
source: Hence, H2A variants appear to be important in shaping the deposition of histone modifications and defining chromatin states.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Chromatin writers and erasers operate with different affinities and efficacies based on the H2A variants in the nucleosome.
source: Overall, our observations suggest that chromatin writers and erasers operate with different affinities and efficacies based on the H2A variants in the nucleosome, an idea that is supported by previous reports.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the data presented in the manuscript and previous reports.

claim: The inhibition of the H2B ubiquitin ligase by the H2A.Z tail is sufficient to explain the anticorrelation between H2Bub and H2A.Z over gene bodies.
source: The inhibition of the H2B ubiquitin ligase by the H2A.Z tail (Surface et al., 2016) is sufficient to explain the anticorrelation between H2Bub and H2A.Z over gene bodies.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Surface et al., 2016.

claim: H2A.Z is the major substrate for H2AK121Ub deposited by PRC1.
source: H2A.Z is the major substrate for H2AK121Ub deposited by PRC1, as indicated by their co-occurrence within chromatin states as well as previous biochemical analyses (Gómez-Zambrano et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by the chromatin state analysis and a citation to Gómez-Zambrano et al., 2019.

claim: PRC2 strongly prefers arrays of H2A.Z as a substrate.
source: PRC2 strongly prefers arrays of H2A.Z as a substrate (Wang et al., 2018), thus supporting the link between H2A.Z and H3K27me3 (Carter et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Wang et al., 2018 and Carter et al., 2018.

claim: The nature of the H2A variant controls the activity of the machinery that either deposits or erases the histone modifications.
source: We propose to expand these examples to the more general idea that the nature of the H2A variant controls the activity of the machinery that either deposits or erases the histone modifications.
evidence: This is a speculative proposal based on the data and previous examples.

claim: Such a model would explain the importance of histone variants in the establishment of chromatin states.
source: Such a model would explain the importance of histone variants in the establishment of chromatin states.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the proposed model.

claim: In mammalian cells, there is a broad maintenance of the patterns of H3 modifications by recycling H3 and H4 at the replication fork.
source: In mammalian cells, there is a broad maintenance of the patterns of H3 modifications by recycling H3 and H4 at the replication fork (Reverón-Gómez et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Reverón-Gómez et al., 2018.

claim: As plant cells divide, H3.1 sustains the deposition of H3K27me3 and H3K27me1.
source: As plant cells divide, H3.1 sustains the deposition of H3K27me3 (Jiang and Berger, 2017) and H3K27me1 (Jacob et al., 2014)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Jiang and Berger, 2017 and Jacob et al., 2014.

claim: H3.1 provides a positive feedback loop to sustain the polycomb repressive state and constitutive heterochromatin in dividing cells.
source: thus providing a positive feedback loop to sustain the polycomb repressive state and constitutive heterochromatin in dividing cells, respectively.
evidence: This is an inference based on the role of H3.1 in maintaining H3K27me3 and H3K27me1.

claim: The recycling of H2A-H2B after replication provides another positive feedback loop to maintain the patterns of H2A variants in mammalian cells.
source: Recent data in mammalian cells show that the recycling of H2A-H2B after replication provides another positive feedback loop to maintain the patterns of H2A variants (Flury et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Flury et al., 2023.

claim: Replication-dependent maintenance mechanisms no longer operate in non-dividing cells, providing opportunities for changing the allocation of chromatin states.
source: Such replication-dependent maintenance mechanisms no longer operate in non-dividing cells, providing opportunities for changing the allocation of chromatin states.
evidence: This is an inference based on knowledge of replication-dependent mechanisms.

claim: The positive feedback loops that maintain histone modifications become inactive and reversion to active chromatin states becomes possible by the deposition of H3.3 and eviction of H2A.Z by INO80 in response to temperature or to light.
source: The positive feedback loops that maintain histone modifications become inactive and reversion to active chromatin states becomes possible by the deposition of H3.3 and eviction of H2A.Z by INO80 in response to temperature (Zhao et al., 2023) or to light (Willige et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Zhao et al., 2023 and Willige et al., 2023.

claim: Mechanisms coupling H3.3 and H2A.Z dynamics are likely general for the regulation of responsive genes that are covered with facultative chromatin states.
source: Mechanisms coupling H3.3 and H2A.Z dynamics are likely general for the regulation of responsive genes that are covered with facultative chromatin states (Long et al., 2023).
evidence: This is a speculative claim ('likely general') supported by a citation to Long et al., 2023.

claim: On expressed genes, acetylated histones assist in the docking of the chromatin remodeler SWI2/SNF2-related 1 (SWR1), which deposits H2A.Z at the transcription start sites (TSS) of expressed genes.
source: Conversely, on expressed genes, acetylated histones assist in the docking of the chromatin remodeler SWI2/SNF2-related 1 (SWR1), which deposits H2A.Z at the transcription start sites (TSS) of expressed genes (Aslam et al., 2019; Bieluszewski et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Aslam et al., 2019 and Bieluszewski et al., 2022.

claim: A relative enrichment of H3.1 with constitutive heterochromatin modifications were previously noted and confirmed in our study.
source: A relative enrichment of H3.1 with constitutive heterochromatin modifications (Johnson et al., 2004) were previously noted and confirmed in our study.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Johnson et al., 2004 and data in the current study.

claim: The preferred substrate for the deposition of the heterochromatic mark H3K27me1 is H3.1.
source: Accordingly, the preferred substrate for the deposition of the heterochromatic mark H3K27me1 is H3.1 (Jacob et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Jacob et al., 2014.

claim: A relationship between H3.3 and H3K36me1/2 was observed, pointing to a possible preference of H3.3 for the deposition of H3K36me or for the demethylation of H3K36me3.
source: We also observed a relationship between H3.3 and H3K36me1/2, pointing to a possible preference of H3.3 for the deposition of H3K36me or for the demethylation of H3K36me3.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation ('possible preference') based on the observed relationship.

claim: It is becoming apparent that the dynamics of H3.3 and H2A.Z are coordinated in Arabidopsis and mammals.
source: In addition, it is becoming apparent that the dynamics of H3.3 and H2A.Z are coordinated in Arabidopsis (Zhao et al., 2023) and mammals (Yang et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Zhao et al., 2023 and Yang et al., 2022.

claim: As yet unknown mechanisms link the deposition of H2A and H3 variants, resulting in specific types of nucleosomes that are sufficient to orchestrate the deposition of PTMs in distinct chromatin states.
source: We thus propose that as yet unknown mechanisms link the deposition of H2A and H3 variants, resulting in specific types of nucleosomes that are sufficient to orchestrate the deposition of PTMs in distinct chromatin states.
evidence: This is a speculative proposal based on the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: These mechanisms will be read, interpreted, and further modified by silencing mechanisms in heterochromatin and the transcriptional machinery in euchromatin, leading to a changing chromatin landscape responding to the activity of the cell and its responses to the environment.
source: These will be read, interpreted, and further modified by silencing mechanisms in heterochromatin and the transcriptional machinery in euchromatin, leading to a changing chromatin landscape responding to the activity of the cell and its responses to the environment.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of how chromatin states are maintained and modified.
